# Results — Study 757 (Cass-Freight)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The **Cass Freight Index** — the
freight-macro world's favourite "real-economy leading indicator" — tested as a signal for
forward equity returns. Cass's monthly shipments series is not freely API-available, so we
use a **hardcoded, cited, APPROXIMATE monthly proxy** (annual anchors interpolated, base
Jan-1990 ≈ 1.00; the year-over-year expansion/contraction shape is the load-bearing fact),
and align it to **real** SPY and IYT month-end closes (yfinance). We then ask whether freight,
known only after Cass publishes it, **leads** the market — and whether an overlay built on it
beats buy-and-hold. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Freight signal | Cass Freight Index (Shipments) — **hardcoded, cited, APPROXIMATE PROXY**; FRED mirror `FRGSHPUSM649NCIS` |
| Real tapes | yfinance month-end adjusted closes: **SPY** (1993→), **IYT** iShares Transportation (2004→) |
| Window | 1999-06-30 → 2026-06-30 (**325** month-ends; **27.0** years); IYT sub-window from 2004-01 (**270** months); as-of **2026-06-30** |
| Freight signal | year-over-year growth of the proxy; "expanding" = YoY > 0; mean **−0.001**, std **0.050**, **50%** of months expanding |
| Entry / lag | **2-month** lag = **1 month publication** (Cass prints the reference month mid-next-month) **+ 1 month execution**; documented once, applied once |
| Costs | timing overlay charges 10 bps one-way per turn; SPY/IYT **price-only** (adjusted closes) |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The freight series is an explicit
> **approximate proxy**, not Cass's licensed tape. The verdict does **not** hinge on its
> exact levels: it hinges on (a) the **sign of the lead-lag** — which orders freight *after*
> equities regardless of the proxy's decimals — and (b) the fact that the conditional excess
> is small/insignificant on SPY and **negative** on the freight-sensitive sector (IYT). If
> anything the proxy is *generous* to the claim: real, revised freight prints arrive later and
> noisier than a smooth interpolated path.

## The signal — forward returns after 'freight expanding' (YoY > 0) vs the base rate

2-month lag; the unconditional column is *all* overlapping forward windows over the same tape
(the honest base rate). Welch *t* compares the conditional mean to the unconditional mean; the
placebo *p* is the share of 20,000 random same-size date draws whose mean forward return
**beats** the expanding-month set.

**SPY** (broad market, 325 months):

| horizon | n expanding | cond. mean | cond. win | base mean | base win | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | 157 | **+0.96%** | 69% | +0.77% | 63% | **+0.49** | 0.298 |
| 3-month  | 157 | **+2.90%** | 74% | +2.33% | 70% | **+0.91** | 0.167 |
| 6-month  | 157 | **+5.69%** | 81% | +4.71% | 73% | **+1.09** | 0.130 |
| 12-month | 157 | **+10.57%** | 86% | +9.62% | 78% | **+0.73** | 0.244 |

**IYT** (transports — the sector freight should move most, 270 months):

| horizon | n expanding | cond. mean | cond. win | base mean | base win | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | 126 | +0.85% | 61% | +0.98% | 61% | **−0.21** | 0.596 |
| 3-month  | 126 | +2.79% | 62% | +2.90% | 63% | **−0.11** | 0.550 |
| 6-month  | 126 | +5.53% | 71% | +5.77% | 69% | **−0.18** | 0.575 |
| 12-month | 126 | +9.38% | 70% | +11.12% | 74% | **−0.94** | 0.837 |

Read it carefully. A tradable leading indicator would want a *large, significant* positive
excess. On SPY we get a **small, insignificant** bump — the strongest is a 6-month **t = 1.09**
(placebo *p* = 0.13), nowhere near the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar. On **IYT — the very sector freight
is supposed to lead — the excess is *negative* at every horizon** (12-month conditional
+9.4% vs a +11.1% base rate, *t* = −0.94): you would have done *worse* owning transports when
freight was expanding. The freight cycle is not front-running the market.

## Lead-lag — the decisive myth-check: stocks lead freight, not the other way round

Cross-correlation of the monthly **change** in freight YoY at month *t* with the equity return
at month *t + k*. `k > 0` ⇒ freight **leads** stocks (what a leading indicator needs);
`k < 0` ⇒ stocks **lead** freight.

| tape | peak lag *k*\* | peak corr | mean \|corr\| when *stocks* lead (k<0) | mean \|corr\| when *freight* leads (k>0) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY** | **−3** | +0.222 | **0.117** | 0.063 |
| **IYT** | **−3** | +0.238 | **0.126** | 0.065 |

The cross-correlation peaks at **k = −3** for both tapes: freight moves most in step with the
equity return of **three months earlier**. The "stocks lead freight" mass (k < 0) is roughly
**2×** the "freight leads stocks" mass (k > 0). Whatever information the freight cycle carries,
the market has it first — freight is a *coincident-to-lagging* read of a turn equities already
made. **The "leading indicator" claim is busted.**

## Tradability — the overlay *loses* to buy-and-hold on both tapes

Hold the tape when freight (known two months earlier) is expanding; otherwise cash (long/flat)
or short (long/short). 10 bps one-way per turn; **price-only** (no cash yield credited while
flat — which *flatters* the overlay).

| tape · rule | exposure | turns | net ann. | **net Sharpe** | buy-&-hold Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY** long / flat  | 48% | 10 | +5.3% | **0.59** | **0.61** |
| **SPY** long / short | 100% | 21 | +1.4% | **0.09** | **0.61** |
| **IYT** long / flat  | 47% | 8 | +5.3% | **0.42** | **0.58** |
| **IYT** long / short | 100% | 17 | −1.0% | **−0.05** | **0.58** |

Every overlay underperforms simply holding — even crediting it **zero** opportunity cost while
in cash. The long/flat SPY rule (0.59) trails buy-and-hold (0.61); on IYT the gap is wider
(0.42 vs 0.58); and betting *against* the tape on contraction months collapses to **0.09**
(SPY) / **−0.05** (IYT) — because freight contractions (2009, 2020) bracket exactly the market
*bottoms* you most wanted to own. There is no version of this that beats buy-and-hold.
**MIRAGE.**

## Robustness — flat-to-negative in the threshold

| 'expanding' threshold | n events | cond. 12m mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| −0.02 (loose) | 192 | +10.0% | **+0.29** | 0.383 |
| **0.00** (sign) | 157 | +10.6% | **+0.73** | 0.244 |
| +0.02 (strict) | 112 | +8.1% | **−1.13** | 0.833 |

Loosening the cutoff washes the *t* toward zero; tightening it turns the excess **negative**.
There is no threshold at which the signal clears *t* = 2.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and a flat signal stays flat

On a deterministic monthly series (AR(1) freight-YoY + SPY-like price) with a **planted**
forward edge (next-return loaded on freight two months earlier):

| planted edge | n expanding | cond. 6m mean | base 6m mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 227 | +7.56% | +7.31% | **+0.24** | 0.374 |
| **0.05** (large edge) | 227 | +42.94% | +29.94% | **+4.68** | **0.000** |

With **no** planted edge the test stays near zero (it cannot manufacture significance from a
noise signal). A genuine planted edge drives *t* to **4.68** and the placebo *p* to **0.000**
— the inference detects a real forward edge when one exists. The machinery is unbiased, so the
real-tape *t* of ~1.1 (SPY) / negative (IYT) is what an *absent* edge looks like, not a broken
detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** After the publication+execution lag, "freight expanding" leaves at best a
  **small, insignificant** positive drift on SPY (strongest *t* = 1.09 at 6m, placebo
  *p* = 0.13; **fails t ≥ 2**) and a **negative** excess on IYT — the freight-sensitive sector
  it should predict best. Survivorship-free; the named structural fact is the **lead-lag
  sign**: the cross-correlation peaks at *k* = −3, i.e. **stocks lead freight** by ~3 months.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A "own-when-freight-expands" overlay earns a **lower Sharpe than
  buy-and-hold** on both tapes (SPY 0.59 vs 0.61; IYT 0.42 vs 0.58), and the long/short
  version collapses (0.09 / −0.05) because freight contractions bracket the market bottoms.
  No NAV-scale edge.
- **Leads the cycle? — BUSTED.** The headline claim — freight *leads* the economy and the
  market — inverts on the tape: equities lead the freight index by about a quarter. "Watch the
  freight" watches the past.
